title: Battle Reel of the Stork-Rider
brief: Battle music for a fantasy story played by a folk band, not an orchestra: fiddle, a wind instrument (clarinet), plucked strings (strumstick, archtop guitar, folk harp), upright bass and hand drums. Fast and driving, about three minutes. The fight changes sides more than once: a running reel, a heavier stamping section and a moment of held breath, the tune passing from instrument to instrument, ending on a blow. One-shot cue, not a loop; delivered as master, MP3, MIDI and stems.

sections.intent: The band strikes in on E minor; the fiddle hovers on B over drum, bass and guitar chops.
The stork-rider's reel: the fiddle states the A-strain twice (E Dorian), running eighths.
The tune passes to the clarinet for the B-strain (warm borrowed G, C, D); the fiddle joins a third below.
The goblins take the field: E Freygish, 3+3+2 stamps, cello and bass riff; clarinet then fiddle carry the prickly tune.
The stork fights back: the strumstick takes the A-strain over harp and fiddle chops, then fiddle and clarinet in thirds.
Held breath: drips on the harp, melting chords sliding down by semitones, the clarinet's snail spiral, a heartbeat drum, then a roll.
The goblins surge: fiddle and clarinet in octaves on the prickly tune, then the cello takes it low; C#7 swings the key.
The final reel a whole step up (F# Dorian): fiddle and clarinet in unison on the A-strain, the stamp's accents in the drums.
High point: the clarinet's B-strain peaks on C#6 under the fiddle's E6, the cello sings a counter-line, every part plays.
The A-strain one last time with the 3+3+2 stamps taken into the reel.
Stop-time stabs, a run up with one beat of silence, and the blow on F#.

association.whole: At the edge of a papaya grove, where the marsh meets the village, a stork-rider guards a child asleep in a reed cot. Hedge-goblins with prickly backs waddle up out of the mud in stamping ranks, bracelets of snail shells rattling on their wrists. The stork hovers and strikes and the reel runs; the goblins stamp back in their crooked mode; the fight swings twice. In the hush between, rain drips from the thatch, the goblin shaman's licorice-black charm melts in the fire and a snail-slow spell coils round the cot, until the village carver steps out and ends it with one blow of a chisel.

plan.identity: A reel that is fought over: the stork's running E Dorian tune and the goblins' 3+3+2 Freygish stamp trade the field, the tune handed from fiddle to clarinet to strumstick to cello, until the reel, a step higher, swallows the stamp and a single blow ends it.

high_point.means: key lifted a whole step to F# Dorian the section before; every part sounds; the clarinet's B-strain peaks on C#6 under the fiddle's E6, the highest note of the piece; the cello's counter-line enters; claps and darbuka on top of the reel drum

the tune passes to the plucked strumstick over harp and fiddle chops; the reel returns

the stamp returns heavier: fiddle and clarinet in octaves, then the cello takes the tune
a whole step higher, F# Dorian; the stamp's accents in the reel drum
the high point: every part plays, the peak notes, the cello's counter-line
the A-strain one last time with the 3+3+2 stamps in drums and cello

decisions: style: primary folk/celtic for what the piece runs on, the reel (rhythm), the fiddle tune in AABB strains (melody) and the frame drum in the bodhran's place. Timbre is borrowed from folk/klezmer because the brief's wind instrument is a clarinet here (the 'licorice stick' of the piece's words) beside a cello and a plucked bass, the klezmer band of the map. Harmony is borrowed from folk/klezmer because the Celtic entry has no source for harmony, and klezmer's accompaniment from bare octaves (the stamp riff of cello and bass) to a second violin's partial chords (the fiddle_sp chops) is what this band plays.

tempo: the Celtic entry has no source for tempo; 168 BPM is the piece's choice from the brief (fast and driving): running eighths at 5.6 notes a second, within what the VSCO solo violin (attack about 20 ms) articulates.
form: the Celtic entry has no source for form; the piece's own, from the brief and the story: reel, stamp, reel, held breath, stamp, final reel a step up, blow.

rhythm of the stamps: the 3+3+2 grouping is the piece's own choice for the goblins' waddle, written as this piece's rhythm rather than as a klezmer bulgar (the rhythm axis is governed by the Celtic entry).
mix: no source read for the Celtic mix; bus chain with the rules of version 2, -14 LUFS.

stand-ins: the vcsl_world strumstick for the bouzouki, banjo or mandolin the banks lack; the vcsl_world frame drums for the bodhran; the vcsl_world folk harp for the Celtic harp (and the klezmer cimbalom's place); the guitar_shiny archtop (microphone) as the band's rhythm guitar; the bass_sneaky upright for the contrabass.

key: E Dorian for the reels (the fiddle's open E and B strings ring in the bracelet figure), E Freygish on the same tonic for the stamps, F# Dorian for the final reel (a whole-step lift into the high point).

vertical: the minor seconds and ninths left are all the stamp's prickle: the tune's F (the Freygish flat second, each time a neighbour or passing note between E and G# or E and D) over the stamped E of bass and cello. That rub is what the goblins' mode is made of here. The accidental ones in the reels and the hush were removed: guitar pushes are power chords, harp drips moved off the held notes, the bracelet plays C instead of B over the C chord.

outside_chord.melody: two kinds remain, both meant. The strumstick's bracelet rings its drone strings E5 and B4 over every chord of the reel, as a dulcimer's open drones ring (the ring of the bracelet), and the goblins' tune leaps the augmented second F-G# (F5 up to G#5, G#5 down to F5), the step that names the Freygish mode. Where a fiddle or clarinet note outside the chord was an accident it was rewritten: A-strain bar 4, the B-strain endings, harmony lines taken from chord tones on the beats, Em7 written where the tune outlines it.

parallels: what remains is meant: doublings (fiddle and clarinet in octaves in stamp_2, the strumstick an octave under the tune and the clarinet in unison in the final reel, bass and cello in octaves on the C#7 riff), the bracelet's drone strings crossing the tune's own E and B, and the hush's melt, where cello and fiddle slide down by semitones in fifths and octaves over the bass (C-G, B-F#, Bb-F, A-E) as one melting block. 24 bass notes in the reels were moved to other chord tones to leave the tune's octaves.

revision_history.what: r1 measured the frame drum as the loudest stem and the leads 3-4 dB under the band in the reels, a very dry mix (C80 +25.7 dB) and half the power in 60-250 Hz: frame drum -3 dB, fiddle and clarinet +1.5 dB, hand percussion +2 dB, reverb sends +2 to +5 dB, the guitar's low voicings moved up with a 90 Hz high-pass; in the hush the clarinet's spiral raised and the held fiddle and cello lowered

r2's stem receipt showed the clarinet slurring 422 of 465 notes: its -50 ms offset is left out of legato notes, so each gap after a slur fell under the 20 ms legato threshold and the slurs chained. Offset -20 ms and tongued eighths at gate 0.72 bring back its tonguing. The review asked about the guitar's 90 Hz high-pass on the blow's F#2, and analyze put the coda guitar level with the tune: the blow's guitar chord starts on F#3, push chords stay above C3, the coda guitar plays 12 velocity lower
